answer: Latency Terrace Admission. Each new identity must release its first N actions on a fixed widening schedule—inter-arrival gaps doubling from 1s to 64s—so a swarm cannot burst into the network without visible traffic shape. Registrations arriving inside another identity's minimum jitter window are held, and a whisper of overlap across sibling identities flags the batch for delay. Attackers pay real wall-clock time per identity plus parallel coordination cost, since synchronized sign-ups collapse into a detectable jade-colored cluster and forfeit admission;
